clue.text: Become a member, we are all in the same position

definitions.meaning: to sign up and enrol in a society

definitions.text: we are all in the same position
definitions.meaning: a rueful idiom said to someone sharing the same misfortune

explanation.surface: An invitation to sign up, since everyone already shares the same plight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means enrolling in a society, and idiomatically it is a sympathetic remark that others suffer the same trouble.

clue.text: Lawful entitlement? Precisely

parts.note: just means fair or lawful
a right is an entitlement

explanation.surface: A question about legal claims answered with a crisp one-word agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites reading the first two words as a phrase meaning a legal claim; each word in fact supplies half the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exactly as it should be is precisely so, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Some find Wellingborough is a good place to abide in

definitions.text: is a good place to abide in

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A recommendation of the Northamptonshire town Wellingborough as a pleasant place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellingborough is a market town in Northamptonshire, England; the definition is a phrase meaning to dwell within.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell within somewhere is to abide or live in it.

clue.text: Entrance bride being carried over it

definitions.text: Entrance bride being carried over it

parts.words: Entrance bride being carried over it
parts.note: the doorway sill of a house, over which a groom traditionally carries his new wife

explanation.surface: A newlywed carried across the doorstep of her new home.
explanation.definitionFit: The sill of a doorway is the entrance a groom carries his bride across by custom.

clue.text: In Bethel I hurried after a Job's comforter

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning three of them

explanation.surface: Someone rushed through the biblical town of Bethel chasing one of Job's visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical Book of Job names the young man who rebukes Job after his three friends; a Job's comforter is one whose consolation makes things worse.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament this young speaker joins Job's friends in offering unhelpful counsel.

clue.text: More vigorous passion? That's right

parts.note: lust is strong passion
i.e., from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone asks if greater vigour comes from passion, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' stands for the abbreviation i.e. (that is), not a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty means hearty and robust, so its comparative is more vigorous.

clue.text: There might be a refusal at the feast

parts.note: taken as written
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: At a banquet someone might decline an invitation.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'There might be a refusal' as the phrase BE A NO, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is British slang for a celebration or party with plenty to eat and drink.

clue.text: Given ill-treatment?

parts.note: read not as abused but as given medicine as treatment for an illness

explanation.surface: A question about someone who has been treated badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient given a measured amount of medicine for sickness has been dosed.

clue.text: Bowler in the van

parts.note: a cricket bowler delivers the ball, and a courier drives a van dropping off parcels

explanation.surface: A cricketer, or a bowler hat, sitting in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket each ball bowled is called a delivery, so the clue's 'Bowler' is a man who makes deliveries, as is the van driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A courier who drops off goods from a van is this, and a cricket bowler makes deliveries too.

clue.text: Place in office again long straps in front

indicators.note: in front means the straps word comes before the long word

parts.note: reins are the long straps used to guide a horse
tall means long or high

explanation.surface: A description of lengthy harness straps placed at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone to a post is to set them up in it once more.

clue.text: Vulture or grey mare, Mel discovered

indicators.note: discovered in the sense of dis-covered, laid open and rearranged, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Mel found that a grey horse was really a vulture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' is the anagram signal on GREYMAREMEL. The bearded vulture of mountain ranges goes by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded vulture of the Alps and Himalayas is known by this name.

clue.text: Bounty, a big vessel

parts.note: large means big
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: HMS Bounty described as a sizeable ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the famous ship Bounty, but bounty here means generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse, also spelt this way, is generous giving, a synonym of bounty.

clue.text: Dress or undress

definitions.meaning: dress ... is the formal outfit of the armed forces; also clothing in general
undress in military use is the everyday, less formal outfit worn by service personnel

explanation.surface: A choice between putting on clothes or taking them off.
explanation.walkthrough: Military parlance has both full dress and undress versions of service clothing, so the apparent opposites define the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Service personnel wear formal and everyday versions of their official outfit, called dress and undress.

clue.text: Watching American soldier in house the French leave

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the shortened house
leave means the French article departs from the house word

parts.note: a villa is a house
la is French for the
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A GI keeps watch in a house while the French depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' drops the French article from the house, and 'in' then lodges the soldier inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of staying awake keeping watch, so watching fits as a noun.

clue.text: Mother wisely included it-or else!

indicators.note: included says the answer is held within the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A mother's threat delivered wisely, ending with a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise is a conjunction meaning if not, the same as or else.

clue.text: Oh, I'd claim that it could be murderous

indicators.note: could be means the words before may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a thing might be deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclined to kill people, the adjective from the killing of a person, so murderous.

clue.text: Wandering waywardly in it with hesitation and a book

indicators.note: waywardly means going astray, so the two short words are jumbled

parts.note: the four letters are the fodder
er is a sound of hesitation
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone wanders off course, hesitating, with a book in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling from place to place, roaming, is a synonym of wandering.

clue.text: Cad took mother to an overseas port

parts.note: a rotter is a cad, an old-fashioned word for a scoundrel
a dam is an animal mother

explanation.surface: A scoundrel whisks his mother away to a foreign harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took' is just a link word between the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: This Dutch city is one of the busiest seaports in Europe, overseas from Britain.

clue.text: Ernest, a confused oriental

indicators.note: confused means the letters of the name and the a are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Ernest is bewildered, mistaken for someone from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and this adjective both mean from or of the East.

clue.text: Support for an injured member

parts.note: member read as a limb: a cloth loop around the neck cradles a hurt arm

explanation.surface: Help offered to a club member who has been hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken arm is held in a looped bandage hung from the neck.

clue.text: Blazer for old Penny to have at the end of the day

parts.note: the sun is a blazer, something that blazes
D was the abbreviation for a penny in pre-1971 British coinage
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Swapping a blazer for a penny at the close of day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blazer' is not a jacket but something blazing. Before 1971 British pennies were written d, from the Latin denarius.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunset, the time the light fades, marks the close of daytime.

clue.text: Ill-treats you and me in vandalised semis

indicators.note: in places the pronoun inside the rearranged houses
vandalised means smashed up, so the letters of the houses are rearranged

parts.note: us means you and me

explanation.surface: Two people are mistreated inside wrecked semi-detached houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalised' scrambles the houses into MISES, and 'in' wraps that round the pronoun. A semi is a British semi-detached house.
explanation.definitionFit: To misuse is to treat wrongly or abuse, a synonym of ill-treat.

clue.text: Play guitar in a way that's unusual

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
rum is British slang for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: Someone plays the guitar in an odd style.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old British slang for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep the fingers across guitar strings is the standard way of playing chords.

clue.text: Case in flight?

parts.note: not luggage on a plane but a step within a flight of steps, which with case makes a ...

explanation.surface: A suitcase travelling on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step is one of many in a flight, and a staircase holds them.

clue.text: Girl to lament going round the factory

indicators.note: going round means the lament word encircles the girl

parts.note: to cry is to lament
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl weeps as she walks around a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant where food is sealed in tins is a kind of factory.

clue.text: Nanny rearranged for us a minder

indicators.note: rearranged means the letters of the three words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A childcare worker has been reorganised to look after us.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after children is a nanny, an exact synonym.

clue.text: From Cremona I returned exalted

indicators.note: From says the answer is taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone back from the Italian city of Cremona in high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' looks like a reversal signal, but it is just part of the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking on air means elated, and exalted is used for that uplifted feeling.

clue.text: It's a small world

parts.note: not the idiom about coincidences but literally a tiny world orbiting the sun, such as an asteroid

explanation.surface: The saying uttered on bumping into an acquaintance far from home.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky body circling the sun, a tiny world of its own.
